title: Accounting Standard 14 Accounting for Amalgamations
outcomes: Distinguish amalgamations in the nature of merger and purchase.
Apply the pooling of interests and purchase methods.
Treat goodwill, capital reserve and statutory reserves, and give disclosures.

meta.exam_tip: Test the five merger conditions first; then compute consideration and choose the method.

concepts.title: Amalgamation and its two types
body: An amalgamation is a merger under the Companies Act or other law in which one company joins another or two or more form a new one. The transferor company is absorbed; the transferee company receives it.
An amalgamation in the nature of merger meets all five conditions in the table; otherwise it is an amalgamation in the nature of purchase.

A merger is a genuine pooling of shareholders' interests and businesses; a purchase is in effect one company acquiring another, after which the transferor's shareholders may not keep a proportionate share.
concepts.analogy: If the shareholders and business genuinely continue together, it is a merger; otherwise it is a purchase.
concepts.work: If 15% of the transferor's shareholders take cash instead of shares, the deal is a purchase.

head: Merger condition
Meaning
rows: Every asset and liability of the transferor becomes the transferee's
Holders of at least 90% of the transferor's equity (by face value), other than the transferee itself, become its shareholders
Consideration to them is equity shares of the transferee, apart from cash for fractions
The transferor's business is intended to be carried on
No change in book values except to unify accounting policies
blocks.title: Amalgamation in the nature of merger

concepts.title: Purchase consideration
body: Purchase consideration is the total of shares and other securities issued and cash or other assets paid by the transferee to the shareholders of the transferor.

It is computed by the net payment method (sum of payments to shareholders) or the net assets method (assets taken over less liabilities, at agreed values). Payments to the transferor's debenture holders and other creditors are not part of it.
Shares and securities issued are valued at fair value; non-cash assets given at their fair values. Adjustments for contingencies are included when probable and reliably estimable.
concepts.analogy: Consideration is what the transferor's shareholders get — nothing else.
concepts.work: Debentures of the transferor replaced by the transferee's debentures are a liability taken over, not consideration.

concepts.title: Pooling of interests method
body: The pooling of interests method is used for an amalgamation in the nature of merger.
Assets, liabilities and reserves (whether capital or revenue) of the transferor are recorded at their existing carrying amounts, after adjustments only to bring accounting policies into line.
The identity of reserves is preserved. The difference between the share capital issued (plus other consideration) and the transferor's share capital is adjusted in reserves.
concepts.analogy: In a merger, both books are simply added together.
concepts.work: A transferor's securities premium appears as securities premium in the merged company.

concepts.title: Purchase method, goodwill and capital reserve
body: The purchase method is used for an amalgamation in the nature of purchase.

Assets and liabilities are recorded at existing carrying amounts or at fair values (allocating consideration to individual identifiable assets and liabilities). Reserves of the transferor other than statutory reserves are not carried over.

Excess of consideration over net assets is goodwill, amortised systematically over its useful life — normally not exceeding five years unless a longer period can be justified. A shortfall is credited to capital reserve.
concepts.analogy: In a purchase, the buyer records what it got at value and the price difference as goodwill or capital reserve.
concepts.work: Paying ₹50 lakh for net assets worth ₹42 lakh creates goodwill of ₹8 lakh.

concepts.title: Statutory reserves and other matters
body: Under the purchase method, statutory reserves of the transferor (those required by law to be kept for a period, such as certain tax-related reserves) are preserved: they are recorded in the transferee's books with a corresponding debit to "Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve", shown as a separate line, and both are reversed when the requirement ends.
If an amalgamation takes place after the year end but before the Board approves the statements, it is disclosed under AS 4 but not incorporated.

Disclose: names and nature of business of the companies, effective date, method of accounting, particulars of the scheme; for mergers, shares issued and the difference treatment; for purchases, consideration and goodwill or capital reserve with the amortisation period.
concepts.analogy: Reserves the law requires to be kept survive even a purchase.
concepts.work: A statutory reserve of ₹5 lakh shows up in the transferee balanced by an Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve.

illustrations.title: Purchase method and goodwill
illustrations.q: Amrit Ltd. takes over Bindu Ltd. in an amalgamation in the nature of purchase. Bindu's assets at fair value less liabilities are ₹9,00,000. Amrit pays Bindu's shareholders 60,000 equity shares of ₹10 each valued at ₹14, plus ₹1,00,000 in cash. Bindu's debentures are taken over separately. Compute the purchase consideration and goodwill.

solution.text: Payments to debenture holders are not part of purchase consideration. Goodwill is amortised over its useful life, normally not more than five years unless a longer period is justified.

illustrations.title: Pooling of interests
illustrations.q: Chetan Ltd. and Disha Ltd. merge, meeting all conditions of a merger. Disha has share capital ₹5,00,000 and general reserve ₹3,00,000. Chetan issues 55,000 equity shares of ₹10 at par to Disha's shareholders. Show the treatment of the difference.

solution.text: All assets, liabilities and reserves are taken at book values; no goodwill or capital reserve arises.

checks.label: Consideration in equity shares at par (₹)

jobs.title: Accounting for an amalgamation scheme
jobs.situation: Your company is absorbing a group company under an approved scheme; 92% of shareholders accept shares and the rest receive cash.
steps: Compute purchase consideration excluding debenture holders.
Record assets, liabilities and reserves by the right method.
jobs.takeaway: Classification decides the method and the treatment of reserves.

mcqs.q: For an amalgamation in the nature of merger, at least what percentage (by face value) of the transferor's equity shareholders must become shareholders of the transferee?
mcqs.explain: One of the five merger conditions requires holders of at least 90% of the face value of the transferor's equity shares (excluding those held by the transferee) to become shareholders of the transferee. In practice: count acceptances.

mcqs.q: Which method applies to an amalgamation in the nature of merger?
mcqs.explain: Mergers are accounted for by pooling of interests, combining assets, liabilities and reserves at book values. Purchases use the purchase method. In practice: confirm all five conditions first.

mcqs.q: Payment to debenture holders of the transferor company is:
mcqs.explain: Purchase consideration includes only what is paid to the transferor's shareholders. Debentures discharged or exchanged are liabilities taken over, not consideration. In practice: exclude them in the net payment method.

mcqs.q: Under the purchase method, excess of purchase consideration over net assets is:
mcqs.explain: Paying more than the value of net assets acquired creates goodwill, which is amortised; paying less creates capital reserve. In practice: compare consideration with net assets at agreed values.
mcqs.topic: Purchase method, goodwill and capital reserve

mcqs.q: Goodwill arising on amalgamation is normally amortised over:
options: Not more than five years unless a longer period is justified
mcqs.explain: AS 14 requires systematic amortisation over useful life, usually five years at most, unless a longer period is clearly justified. In practice: document the justification.
mcqs.topic: Purchase method, goodwill and capital reserve

mcqs.q: Under pooling of interests, reserves of the transferor are:
mcqs.explain: In a merger all reserves of the transferor, capital or revenue, keep their identity in the transferee's books, after adjusting for any difference between consideration and share capital. In practice: merge reserve heads.

mcqs.q: Net assets taken over ₹25 lakh; consideration ₹22 lakh (purchase method). The difference is:
mcqs.explain: When the consideration is lower than the net assets acquired, the shortfall of ₹3 lakh is credited to capital reserve, not profit and loss. In practice: it is not distributable.
mcqs.topic: Purchase method, goodwill and capital reserve

mcqs.q: Statutory reserves of the transferor under the purchase method are:
options: Recorded with a matching debit to Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve
mcqs.explain: To keep statutory reserves intact as the law requires, they are recorded in the transferee's books with a corresponding debit to Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve, reversed when no longer needed. In practice: show separately.

mcqs.q: An amalgamation is in the nature of purchase if:
options: Any one of the five merger conditions is not met
Shares are issued at a premium
mcqs.explain: Failing any of the five conditions — all assets and liabilities, 90% shareholders, equity-only consideration, business continuity, book values — makes it a purchase. In practice: test each.

mcqs.q: An amalgamation effective after the balance sheet date but before approval of accounts is:
options: Treated as a prior period item
mcqs.explain: Such an amalgamation is a non-adjusting event; it is disclosed but not incorporated in the financial statements of the year just ended. In practice: account for it next year.

questions.q: Amrit Ltd. takes over Bindu Ltd. in an amalgamation in the nature of purchase. Bindu's assets at fair value less liabilities are ₹9,00,000. Amrit pays Bindu's shareholders 60,000 equity shares of ₹10 each valued at ₹14, plus ₹1,00,000 in cash. Bindu's debentures are taken over separately. Compute the purchase consideration and goodwill.

model.text: Payments to debenture holders are not part of purchase consideration. Goodwill is amortised over its useful life, normally not more than five years unless a longer period is justified.

mistakes: Using book values of shares issued.

questions.q: Chetan Ltd. and Disha Ltd. merge, meeting all conditions of a merger. Disha has share capital ₹5,00,000 and general reserve ₹3,00,000. Chetan issues 55,000 equity shares of ₹10 at par to Disha's shareholders. Show the treatment of the difference.

model.text: All assets, liabilities and reserves are taken at book values; no goodwill or capital reserve arises.

checks.label: Consideration in equity shares at par (₹)

summary: Merger: all five conditions; otherwise purchase.
Consideration: to shareholders only; excludes debenture holders.
Pooling: book values, reserves preserved, difference to reserves.
Purchase: book or fair values; only statutory reserves carried.
Excess → goodwill (≤ 5 years); shortfall → capital reserve.
Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve for statutory reserves.
traps: General reserve of the transferor is not carried in a purchase.

viva.q: Name the conditions for an amalgamation in the nature of merger.
viva.model: All assets and liabilities pass; 90% equity holders become shareholders; consideration only in equity shares except cash for fractions; business continues; book values kept except for uniform policies.
The total of shares, securities, cash and other assets given by the transferee to the transferor's shareholders.

viva.q: How does pooling of interests treat reserves?
viva.model: All reserves of the transferor are recorded at book value with their identity preserved; the consideration difference is adjusted in reserves.

viva.q: How is goodwill on amalgamation treated?
viva.model: It is amortised over its useful life, normally within five years unless a longer period is justified.

viva.q: What is the Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve?
viva.model: A debit balance created to match statutory reserves of the transferor carried into the transferee under the purchase method, reversed when the statutory need ends.

cases.title: Ganga Ltd. and Yamuna Ltd.
cases.case: Ganga Ltd. absorbs Yamuna Ltd. Yamuna has equity capital ₹40 lakh, general reserve ₹10 lakh, a statutory investment allowance reserve ₹4 lakh, and net assets at fair value ₹62 lakh. Ganga issues equity shares worth ₹50 lakh and pays ₹8 lakh cash to Yamuna's shareholders. 20% of Yamuna's shareholders opted for cash only.

mcqs.q: The amalgamation is in the nature of:
options: Purchase, as fewer than 90% become shareholders and cash is paid
mcqs.explain: With 20% of shareholders taking cash, the 90% and equity-only conditions fail, so the purchase method applies. In practice: record at fair values.
Consideration is shares ₹50 lakh plus cash ₹8 lakh = ₹58 lakh, all paid to Yamuna's shareholders. In practice: compare with net assets next.

options: Capital reserve ₹4 lakh, and the statutory reserve with an Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve
mcqs.explain: Net assets ₹62 lakh exceed consideration ₹58 lakh, giving capital reserve of ₹4 lakh; the general reserve is not carried over, but the statutory reserve is preserved against an Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve. In practice: disclose both.
